title: feat(spec): the paired .custom package declares an installed object's field-group and tab arrangement
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9JpRoUZGqtwqMU5k7b4C58D)_

Fixes #36498

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: follow-up #36541

## 维护者速读

- 环境管理员可以给已安装软件包里的对象整体重排记录页：把原厂字段挪到别的分组、调换分组顺序、调换或隐藏子表页签；不写这份排布，页面和以前完全一样。
- 属于「记录页标签与分组」专题的第三层（原始软件包、继承软件包之后的环境管理员覆盖），让客户不改原厂包也能按自己的习惯排页面。
- 排错了只影响这一个对象的记录页、表单和预览的摆放，数据不受影响，但把没有默认值的必填字段藏起来会让用户在表单里建不了记录；删掉这份排布或停用环境定制包，页面立刻回到原厂加扩展包的样子。
- 审批这次公开配置格式的新增：对象扩展多了两项只有环境定制包能写的排布设置。

## What changes

The record page is arranged in three layers. The package that owns an object declares `fieldGroups` and `relatedLists`; a package that extends it places what it brings with `place`; this PR adds the third: the object extension of the paired `.custom` package may declare the whole arrangement, over both.

**Spec keys touched** (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, `related-list-entry.ts`, `field-customization.ts`, `kernel/metadata-read-decorations.ts`):

| Key | Change |
|:---|:---|
| `ObjectExtensionSchema.fieldGroups` | New. An array of `ObjectFieldGroupSchema`, the shape an object's `fieldGroups` takes; keys unique. Was refused at parse with a prescription naming `place`. |
| `ObjectExtensionSchema.relatedLists` | New. An array of `ObjectExtensionRelatedListEntrySchema`: a bare name (a child, a relationship, or one of the three built-in tab names) or `{ list, label?, columns?, hidden? }`. Was refused at parse the same way. |
| `ObjectExtensionRelatedListEntryObjectSchema.hidden` | New, on this entry only. `RelatedListEntryObjectSchema` (an object's own entry) still refuses `hidden`, now with a sentence saying where it belongs. |
| `METADATA_READ_DECORATIONS` | `_relatedListsArrangement` added: derived on read, stripped on write, never authorable. |
| `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST` | Unchanged (see `hidden`, below). |

New exports: `CUSTOM_ARRANGEMENT_KEYS`, `extensionArrangementKeys`, `relatedListEntryHidden`, `relatedListNameCovers`, `RELATED_LISTS_ARRANGEMENT_DECORATION`, `RelatedListsArrangement`, `readRelatedListsArrangement`, the two entry schemas and their types.

**Who may write them.** The schema admits the keys on any extension, because a parse does not know the writing package. The writer is judged where the package is known, by one judge (`judgeExtensionArrangement`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-arrangement.ts`) on the `__c` precedent's predicate (`isCustomizationPackage`), at the same doors as the `__c` reservation:

- save, publish and restore of an `object_extension` item (`objectExtensionItemRefusal`): `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400, one issue per key;
- `os validate` and `os build` (`findExtensionArrangementRefusals`, in the validate/build parity roster);
- marketplace install (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`): `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 422 with `details.refusals`.

Each refusal names the key, the object and the package and prescribes `place` with an example entry. An extension that reaches the registry past those doors is skipped by the fold and named in the boot log.

**Which `.custom` package is served.** The doors judge by the suffix; the fold decides by role. It serves only the object's own pair: the `.custom` package of the App the object belongs to, asked of `pairsOf` over the installed manifests (`packages/metadata-core/src/customization-pair-lookup.ts`, the list `isPairOf` tests against). That list is the App's pair first and then, while one is installed, a per-package pair an earlier version created. A `.custom` writer outside the list is skipped and named in the boot log, alone or beside the pair. Where both listed pairs write one key, the App's pair is served and the other is named. Fold order decides nothing (ADR-0146 D2).

**The merge** (`packages/objectql/src/registry-custom-arrangement.ts`, wired into `foldExtendersOntoDefinition` after `applyExtensionPlacements`): the owner's arrangement, then every extension's `place`, then the `.custom` key replaces the result, whole. A key the extension does not write keeps the result of the first two steps. Nothing is merged entry by entry.

- Fields: a field no group lists is not dropped; it shows after the last group. A group that lists `fields` shows exactly its list, so a field of the owner or of another extension that no list names loses a `group` naming such a group, and a listed field's own `group` follows the group that lists it. The served object still passes an object parse.
- Tabs: the served `relatedLists` is the arrangement's shown entries, then the entries of the list it replaced that it does not name (before a trailing approvals / activity-stream run). `{ list, hidden: true }` hides that list, whichever package brings it. What a served `relatedLists` cannot say travels in the `_relatedListsArrangement` read decoration (`{ packageId, hidden, unlisted }`), stamped on the served by-name read and the served object list, not on the execution face. Where the arrangement hides every tab of a declared list, the served list is empty and `unlisted: 'hidden'` beside it says it is still a declared list.
- Removing a key, or uninstalling or disabling the `.custom` package, serves the first two steps again. Nothing is stored in the base or in another package.

**The record page** (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts`, `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts`): both readers read the decoration through `readRelatedListsArrangement`. A list the environment hides is not derived; where the arrangement replaced the automatic tab list, a list no entry names still shows after the listed ones, and so does the attachments tab. An empty served list beside `unlisted: 'hidden'` is read as a declared list that names nothing, so a list the owner hid by leaving it out stays hidden. With no decoration served, both answer exactly as before; each reader's suite ends with a block that pins that against literal values.

**`hidden` on a field did not enter `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST`.** The whitelist's admission test is "display only: never changes what is stored, validated or computed". `FieldSchema.hidden` fails it on three counts: a hidden field is left out of the search companion column (the stored value changes), a form's required check skips it (`required && hidden !== true`, the validation verdict changes), and default search and export columns drop it. So the whitelist is not widened. The explicit arrangement form is a `.custom` field group whose `visibleWhen` is false: `{ key: 'off_page', label: 'Not shown', fields: ['fax'], visibleWhen: 'false' }` keeps a vendor field off the record page and the forms. Two limits, now stated in the key's description, the whitelist's doc comment, the docs page and the changeset:

- It is presentation only, not access control: the field stays readable and writable through the API.
- It is not for a `required` field that has no default: the create form no longer shows the field while the save still requires it, so the form cannot be submitted.

**The per-user tab order still layers on top.** The console keeps each reader's tab order and hidden tabs as a diff over the host's default order (`ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/relatedArrangement.ts`), and the default order is `deriveRelatedLists` over the served object. The environment layer is in the served object, so the reader's order is laid over it unchanged. A list the environment hides is not derived, so a reader's saved arrangement cannot bring it back.

**Docs and changeset**: `content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx` gains "Arranging the whole record page"; `.changeset/36498-custom-package-arrangement.md` (`minor` on the eight packages moved). The changeset no longer says a non-`.custom` writer is refused on every path: where no door judges it, the key is not applied and the boot log names it.

## Tests

The acceptance bullets of the card are reproduced over a base + extension package + `.custom` fixture (`com.vendor.crm`, `com.acme.tax`, `com.vendor.crm.custom`, object `crm_lead`), and the App pair over two installed packages in the HotCRM shape (an App `com.hotcrm` and a module of it, `com.hotcrm.sales`, that owns the object); HotCRM itself is not edited.

| Suite | What it pins |
|:---|:---|
| `packages/objectql/src/registry-custom-arrangement.test.ts` | A base field moved to another group and two groups swapped; an unlisted base field after the last group, in both membership spellings; an extension package's placed field not in the arrangement still shows, last; two tabs swapped and one hidden; an unlisted tab shows last; every tab of a declared list hidden (the owner lists two of its three lists, the arrangement hides both; and the one-entry case): the served list is empty and the read says `unlisted: 'hidden'`; only `relatedLists` written keeps the groups of the first two steps; removing both keys, uninstalling and disabling the pair each restore; a non-`.custom` writer is skipped with a boot-log line naming `place`; a `.custom` package that is not the object's pair is skipped and named, beside the pair and alone; an object a module owns with two `.custom` writers, in both fold orders: the App's pair is served and the other named; an installed per-package pair is read, and comes second to the App's pair; re-fold idempotence. The layout is asserted through `deriveFieldGroupLayout`, the derivation the record page, the forms and the preview share. |
| `packages/objectql/src/protocol-custom-arrangement.test.ts` | Through the real protocol and engine: the pair's save is admitted; the by-name and list reads serve the arrangement and the decoration; the execution face is undecorated; a writable non-`.custom` package's save is refused once (`VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400, `place` named), nothing stored; re-saving without the keys and disabling the pair restore. |
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-arrangement.test.ts` | The judge and the publish-door refusal, with the `.custom` control. |
| `packages/cli/test/validate-build-extension-arrangement.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/extension-arrangement.test.ts` | `os validate` and `os build` each refuse once and name `place`; the `.custom` control passes; the parity roster row. |
| `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-extension-arrangement.test.ts` | Install refuses once (422, `details.refusals`), nothing installed; the `.custom` control installs. |
| `packages/spec/src/data/object-extension-arrangement.test.ts`, `object-extension-place.test.ts` | The two keys' shapes and refusals, `hidden` accepted on the extension entry only, the contradiction and `place`-beside-arrangement refusals, the whitelist unchanged. |
| `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/__tests__/deriveRelatedLists.customArrangement-36498.test.ts`, `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/__tests__/buildDefaultPageSchema.customArrangement-36498.test.ts` | The reader: hidden lists, unlisted-shown, an empty served list beside `unlisted: 'hidden'` (the list the owner left out stays hidden; without the decoration the empty list reads as before), and the pin that nothing moves with no decoration served. |

## Acceptance notes

- **Contract review, first record: three should-fix items, each answered on this head.**
  - Hiding every tab of a declared list revealed the lists the owner hid. Answered in the readers' reading of the decoration, not in the served shape: the fold still serves an empty list, and `unlisted: 'hidden'` beside it now reads as a declared list that names nothing. This was the smaller change: the decoration's shape and the fold's output are as they were, and the documented rule (a list the owner hides by leaving it out stays hidden until the arrangement names it) now holds in the empty case too. Pinned in the fold suite and in both reader suites.
  - The choice among `.custom` writers did not know the App pair. The fold now asks `pairsOf`, never `isCustomizationPairOf`; the arm that served the writer folded last is gone. One call made here: an installed per-package pair of an earlier version is admitted, second to the App's pair, because the lookup module prescribes `isPairOf` / `pairsOf` for every read that serves a package's customizations.
  - The recipe for keeping a base field off the page now states its two limits in the four published places.
- **Carriers of what this PR does not do:**
  - Item 6 of the card, the ADR-0146 D10 note: the row on #36086. An implementation PR does not edit `docs/adr/**`; the sentences this change puts out of step and their replacement wording are in the report.
  - The skills guide for the two keys: #36541.
  - Hiding a built-in tab (attachments, approvals, the activity stream) of an installed object from the environment's layer is not possible as built: `hidden` is for relationship entries, and an unlisted built-in tab shows. A separate finding, which the seat files.
  - Three paths where a non-`.custom` writer's key is only skipped with a boot-log line, where `main` refused it at parse: a code-defined stack that boots without `os validate` or `os build`; a stack that names no package id, which `os validate` passes; and package duplicate and orphan adoption. Nothing is applied on any of them. A follow-up, not a change on this head.
  - The save and install doors could also refuse a `.custom` writer that is not the object's pair: they can read the installed manifests, which the CLI door cannot. As built they judge by the suffix, and the fold skips such a writer with a boot-log line. A follow-up.
  - Editor UI for these keys: the follow-up card, not this PR. Studio shows the merged result because it reads the served object.
- **Calls that stand as built:**
  - Fields: "replaced whole" is read for both membership spellings, so an unlisted field always lands after the last group, never inside a group its owner had named.
  - Tabs: a list the object's owner hides by leaving it out of its own `relatedLists` stays hidden until the arrangement names it; "unlisted shows last" applies to the tabs the first two steps showed.
  - A `place` entry beside the arrangement key that replaces it, in one extension, is refused at parse.
  - A name in a `.custom` arrangement that the object does not have (a field in a group's list, a tab entry) is not judged at `defineStack`, `os validate` or install. The layout derivation and the tab reader skip a name nothing answers to, as they do for an object's own arrangement, so a vendor upgrade that removes a field does not make the environment's next save fail.
- **Overlap**: an open draft PR edits another region of `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (field history defaults); the later lander merges main.
- **Size**: 3,566 changed lines, over the 3000 changed-line human-merge threshold, so it lands as a Tier H surface does.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:

1. `packages/objectql/src/registry-custom-arrangement.ts`, two hunks. `servedWriter`: a writer is admitted when its package is a `.custom` package and is in `pairsOf` of the object's owner, and the served one is chosen by its position in that list; this decides whose arrangement an installed object shows. The field hunk under `// ── fieldGroups`: it rewrites or removes a field's own `group` on the served copy (never on a stored body) so that a listing group shows exactly its list; this decides where an unlisted field lands.
2. `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, the `ObjectExtensionSchema` hunk: the two `guidance` refusals are removed and the keys are admitted on every extension; the writer is refused at the doors instead. Check that every door a package's extension passes is listed above, and the two key descriptions against what the fold does.
3. `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts`, the `naming` line and the final loop: an empty served list beside `unlisted: 'hidden'` becomes an empty naming map, so the loop takes the declared arm and shows only what is named or brought by another package. `hiddenByArrangement` runs before the `!naming` early exit. All of it is inert when `readRelatedListsArrangement` answers `undefined`.

Two-minute check, one command:

```
pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/registry-custom-arrangement.test.ts
```

Expected: 33 cases pass; the case titles read as the card's acceptance bullets and the review's three items.
